What a sourdough starter actually eats

A starter is a community of wild yeast and bacteria living in flour and water. The yeast feeds on the sugars that enzymes release from the flour, and the bacteria turn some of those sugars into the acids that give the bread its tang.

Whole grain flours carry more of both the microbes and the nutrients, so a starter fed with rye or whole wheat tends to wake up faster than one fed only on white flour.

Warmth speeds everything up. A starter that doubles in four hours at a warm kitchen temperature may need twelve in a cold one, so judge it by how it looks rather than by the clock.
